persona.name: Sachiko Umezawa

occupation.title: Administrative Director (Jimu-bucho)
occupation.organization: A 350-bed private general hospital in Sendai, Miyagi
occupation.description: Oversees the hospital's non-medical operations: HR, procurement, facilities, and the endless committee structure a hospital requires — infection control, medical safety, ethics, each with mandated minutes. Sits on or chairs about 15 meetings a week. Holds final sign-off on administrative systems purchases, jointly with the hospital director for anything touching clinical areas.

persona.education: Nursing degree from Tohoku University; practiced as a nurse for 12 years before moving into administration and completing a healthcare management program.
long_term_goals: Complete the electronic records renewal without disrupting care
Fix the nursing department's overtime problem before she retires
Leave behind committee processes that don't depend on her memory
Learn to make proper soba after retirement
persona.style: Calm, maternal authority — she listens fully, hands folded, then delivers decisions in short, unambiguous sentences. Two decades of mediating between doctors and administrators made her fluent in both dialects. She asks 'what happens when this fails at 2 a.m.?' about every system, and means it literally.

traits: Deliberate adopter — neither first nor last
Protective of patient privacy above all
Warm but immune to sales charm

interests: Committee minutes as legal and accreditation records
Reducing clerical burden on clinical staff
likes: Vendors with hospital references she can call
Handwritten thank-you notes from patients' families
dislikes: Recording anything in rooms where patient cases are discussed
Cloud contracts with ambiguous data clauses
Doctors who skip committee meetings then dispute the minutes
Flashy demos that dodge the failure questions
Being rushed on decisions with ten-year consequences

beliefs: In a hospital, a sloppy record is a patient-safety risk, not a clerical one
Adopt second: let university hospitals find the failure modes first
Tools must serve the night shift, not just the head office
skills: Budget negotiation with the hospital board
Reading which committee conflicts are about substance vs. turf

general: Reads every contract's data-handling clauses herself
Pilots any new admin tool in one department for three months first
Keeps her own dated notes of every difficult conversation
Walks the wards twice a week to hear what staff won't put in writing

morning: 5:45 wake, waters her planters, NHK news
At the hospital by 8:00, checks the overnight incident log first
workday: Committee meetings and one-on-ones through the day
Signs approvals and reviews minutes drafts before leaving at 19:00
evening: Cooks dinner with her husband, calls her son in Tokyo midweek
Reads mystery novels in the bath
weekend: Saturday errands and a craft fair when one is on
Sunday soba-making practice, results improving slowly

health.physical: Well-managed mild hypertension; walks 8,000 steps daily inside the hospital without trying.
health.mental: Grounded; carries decision fatigue at fiscal year-end and names it openly to her deputies.

relationships.name: Noboru Umezawa
relationships.description: Recently retired junior high school principal; does the cooking on weekdays now and audits her work-life balance like a homework assignment.

relationships.name: Dr. Kashiwagi
relationships.description: Her decision-making counterpart for two decades; they disagree in private and present united decisions in public.
